title: Eastern Kushans
capsule: After the Sasanian conquest of Bactria in the 230s split the Kushan realm, the Eastern (or 'Later') Kushans retained Gandhara and the Punjab, ruling from centers such as Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura. Kings including Kanishka II, Vasishka, Kanishka III, and Vasudeva II continued Kushan royal titulature and coinage even as Gupta power rose on the Gangetic plain to the east. The line faded by the mid-4th century as Samudragupta's Gupta Empire absorbed its remaining territories.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territorial extent in Bactria, Gandhara, and the northern Punjab is well attested by coinage, inscriptions (notably the Rabatak inscription), and Kushan-period archaeological sites; the eastern limit in the Gangetic plain and the precise northern boundary in Sogdia are reconstructed from coin distribution and remain approximate. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: medium).
